AfterAddedToRoom.maps_to: PunchConstruct.adjust_hp_after_added (monsters/underdocks/punch_construct.py) for the HP reduction, run by CombatState.after_creature_added; PunchConstruct.__init__ for the Artifact (clause 1, the pool-wide deliberate divergence); _PunchOffEncounter.create_monsters (events/punch_off.py) for the per-encounter roll
AfterAddedToRoom.issue: CLOSED 2026-07-29 (round 10, the Tier 1 residue). Clause 2b, both halves. (a) THE STREAM: `_PunchOffEncounter.create_monsters` (events/punch_off.py) now rolls `selection_rng.next_int_range(2, 10)` twice on the per-encounter Rng it was already being handed and ignoring, matching PunchOffEventEncounter.cs:17,:19's two `base.Rng.NextInt(2, 10)` draws (EncounterModel.cs:259-270). It takes 2 draws there and 0 on the shared combat rng, where it took 0 and 2. (b) THE LIFECYCLE SLOT: the reduction is no longer spent at construction. It is stored as `PunchConstruct.starting_hp_reduction` -- the port of the `StartingHpReduction` FIELD (PunchConstruct.cs:60-69) -- and spent by `PunchConstruct.adjust_hp_after_added`, the sim's port of `AfterAddedToRoom`, as `hp = max(1, hp - reduction)` with max_hp untouched (PunchConstruct.cs:71-79). That override now actually RUNS, because `CombatState.after_creature_added` -- built this round as the port of CombatManager.cs:858-867 -- calls `creature.adjust_hp_after_added(...)` as its first statement, which is `await creature.AfterAddedToRoom()`. It used to hang off `_assign_parity_monster_hp`, so it ran on neither the legacy path nor for a mid-combat spawn. This is what unblocks the PARITY path the entry says erased the reduction outright: `_roll_parity_hp`'s `hp = max_hp = rolled` and `PregeneratedEncounter.create_monsters`' identical re-assignment both run BEFORE the fix-up now instead of after it. EXECUTED end to end -- a string-seeded run enters punch_off at floor 7, `GenerateInternalCombatState` pre-rolls [55, 55] (max HP; AfterAddedToRoom has not run on those throwaway creatures), and the rebuilt fight comes out 50/55 and 49/55 with reductions 5 and 6. Exactly once: the per-encounter Rng is re-seeded identically in both passes (`make_encounter_rng(seed, floor, entry)`), so no draw is double-spent. `py audit/tools/monster_probes_b03.py punchoff-hp` still reports hp=53/49 with max_hp=55. Pinned by test/test_tier1_residue.py (4 tests). WAS: RE-OPENED 2026-07-28. Three clauses, three different answers, and only one of them is closed. CLAUSE 2a (WHICH FIELD) IS CLOSED: _PunchOffEncounter.create_monsters (events/punch_off.py:26-33) is now `m.hp = max(1, m.hp - reduction)` with max_hp left at PunchConstruct's flat 55 (punch_construct.py:26-27), matching PunchConstruct.cs:75-78's `SetCurrentHpInternal(Math.Max(1, Creature.CurrentHp - StartingHpReduction))`, which touches MaxHp not at all; `py audit/tools/monster_probes_b03.py punchoff-hp` reports hp=53 max_hp=55 and hp=49 max_hp=55. The NextInt(2, 10) RANGE and the first construct's StartsWithFastPunch flag were already correct. CLAUSE 1 (ArtifactPower 1, PunchConstruct.cs:74, applied from punch_construct.py:39-40 rather than from an add-to-room phase) remains SHARED-FINDINGS section 2's pool-wide deliberate divergence -- see this entry's rationale. CLAUSE 2b IS STILL A GAP, and it is why this entry cannot read 'no live gap': the two reductions are drawn off the WRONG STREAM and, on the parity path, then erased. events/punch_off.py:26 accepts a `selection_rng` argument and IGNORES it, rolling `rng.randint(2, 9)` on the shared combat random.Random at :30, where PunchOffEventEncounter.cs:17,:19 roll `base.Rng.NextInt(2, 10)` twice on the per-encounter EncounterModel Rng (EncounterModel.cs:259-270). The plumbing is already in place and five sibling encounters use it (monsters/glory/scroll_of_biting.py:105-108, monsters/underdocks/corpse_slug.py:84, monsters/overgrowth/slithering_strangler.py:74, monsters/hive/decimillipede.py:156, monsters/overgrowth/slimes.py:190); run.py:1299-1303 builds the stream and combat.py:135-136 passes it into create_monsters, and punch_off is reached through PunchOff.canonical_encounter. Consequences: 0 draws on the per-encounter stream where the game takes 2, 2 extra draws on the shared rng, different construct HP for a given run seed and floor -- and on the parity path the reduction is wiped outright, because create_monsters runs BEFORE CombatState._assign_parity_monster_hp, whose _roll_parity_hp does `creature.hp = creature.max_hp = hp` (combat.py:263), and PregeneratedEncounter.create_monsters does the same at events/_combat_layout.py:73-74. audit/records/event/punch_off.json carries this as two `gap` entries (guard EV-3 and the StartingHpReduction guard, both re-derived 2026-07-28), so binding rule 3 requires the same verdict here rather than a record that reports no gap. THE CORRECT HOME for the reduction is Monster.adjust_hp_after_added -- the sim's port of AfterAddedToRoom, run at combat.py:277-278 AFTER the Niche max-HP roll, exactly where PunchConstruct.cs:70-79 sits. WAS (clause 2a): the reduction was applied to max_hp and hp clamped to it, so a construct the game shows at 46/55 the sim showed at 46/46. Rule 7: sts2_rl/combat.py, sts2_rl/run.py, sts2_rl/events/_combat_layout.py, src/Core/Models/EncounterModel.cs and the five sibling monster modules are cited without being hashed by this record.

It does not: PunchConstruct.cs:77 calls SetCurrentHpInternal, which is the game's own raw current-HP setter for exactly this purpose, so a sim assignment that skips the hooks is faithful to the source here. The divergence recorded on AfterAddedToRoom is about WHICH FIELD is written, not about the hooks the write skips.
